Lower a by = character() join

Source: R/lower.R
lower_cross_by_join.Rd

dplyr runs its ordinary join machinery with a constant key (join_rows(cross = TRUE)), so every x row matches every y row. That is a cartesian product when both sides have rows (gpu_cross_join(), x-major), but an empty side behaves like an outer join: left/full keep x with NA y columns, right/full keep y with NA x columns, inner gives 0 rows; semi returns x iff y has rows, anti the opposite. Row counts are only known here, at execution time, so the empty-side cases are decided in R. Deliberately NOT a hash join on a constant key column (a hash build over n identical keys is quadratic).

Usage

lower_cross_by_join(ast, left_ptr, right_ptr, left_schema, right_schema)

Details

multiple = "first"/"any"/"last" keep y's first/last row for each x row; for right/full the other y rows are then unmatched and appended with NA x columns, like dplyr. relationship/unmatched run through check_join_cardinality() on a diag synthesized from the two row counts; the default relationship is "many-to-many" (no warning).
